title: A $500 colonial costume gig in Worcester and a cancelled job
summary: A Harvard student hires Whaley's four-man band for $500 at a colonial party where they barely play, and later a false telegram cancelling a job is settled by his lawyer.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: And I was playing down on Beech Street, and a Harvard student came in one night and he says, 'hey, how much you charge to play down in Worcester?' I said, '$500,' just like that, see. Now, I didn't know -- I thought he was kidding, see, so I said $500. I had four men there. So about a couple of weeks later, this guy came in, hey, remember what we was talking about? I said, oh, yeah. He said, well, the job is on such-and-such a day.

Now, I had -- he give me a retainer, and I got somebody to take our places for one night. And we went down and hired a car to take us down to Worcester. And this was in May, see. And it was a colonial -- everybody was dressed as a colonial, see.

MR. WHALEY: Colonial dress, and had the wigs on and everything. And you know what? We didn't do much playing down there. The steward came and said, now, you fellows will play over there, and he designated where we would play. And he says, they'll tell you when to play. Now, you want something to eat, you sit down here and eat.

And we ate and drank and played. Didn't play much, because they weren't interested, see. This was just for show, the band was, see. And we went back to Boston and I used to tell the fellows, oh, that was a great outing.
That was a good gig, wasn't it?
Oh, yeah, that was a good gig.
That was good money. A guy used to get ten or 15 dollars a night. You got $500 for five men.

Well, another time, a guy come up to me and asked me if I would play up there in -- oh, somewhere up in the northern part of Massachusetts. And I told him, yeah. I hired a car and we went up there and the man says, what are you doing up here? I says, well, didn't you tell me -- he said I got a telegram saying that everything was off. I said, no, I wrote that everything is on, be up there.

And, sure enough, we went down to the telegraph office and there was the telegram, everything off. I said, that guy was dizzy, whoever signed that. Because -- I came back to New York, I mean, to Boston and I got my lawyer. I had a lawyer from the federal government, Will Schotten. And he said, don't worry about it, Tom. I'll get -- so sure enough, I got all my money back.
That's good. You even remember the lawyer's name from that era.
Yeah, it just come to me, like that.
